client: python-httpx language-neutral probe (not a native client)
environment: local lane Supabase stack argus-native-auth-proof (jwt_expiry=60, confirmations on) + unchanged Argus API; Argus API launched from the fix branch at argus_api_head

results.scenario: Handoff creation over the proposed header transport
results.expected: 201 with handoff_id, expires_at, handoff_secret in JSON; no Set-Cookie reaches the client

results.scenario: Bearer-only sign-in presents the stored handoff in headers
results.expected: 200 with guest_claim; conversation owned by the account; client told to delete its handoff

results.scenario: Response lost after the claim committed; retry with the same stored handoff
results.expected: 200 with the same guest_claim (Argus replay rule applies unchanged)

results.scenario: Wrong account signs in; the session Argus created is returned beside the problem
results.expected: 403 guest_handoff_wrong_destination with a session the app can keep or revoke
results.note: Closes the C7 gap, where a bearer client gets no tokens for a session that exists.

results.scenario: Guest signs up, confirms by email, relaunches with the handoff from secure storage
results.expected: Signup 200 without session; first sign-in after confirmation claims

results.scenario: A tampered secret, and handoff headers sent outside /api/v1/auth
results.expected: Tampered secret refused as guest_handoff_invalid; headers outside the auth path are not forwarded
results.note: The tampered attempt signs the user in (Argus answers the handoff problem after password success), which S4's session-in-body rule covers.

results.scenario: A new install starts a guest through the adapter after other accounts signed in
results.expected: 200 new guest; the proxy never replays another caller's Argus cookie
results.note: Regression for a bug in the first adapter build, caught by iOS I8: its upstream client kept sb-auth-token and a new guest was treated as signed in (409).
